findings.claim: The guard read the serving file with loadCompiledRulesFile and no onWarn callback; that loader turns a JSON parse failure (conflict markers, a BOM, truncation) into a warning and an empty rule set (core compiler.ts:211-219), so a record-managed file that does not parse showed no record rows, the guard passed it, and the compile reloaded it as empty and overwrote it without the record rows (compile.ts:1173-1174, saves at 1319 and 1985); under --refresh-manifest the malformed bytes were hashed into the manifest.
findings.counterexample: Measured by the leg on the worktree's core build with a file holding a conflict marker before a valid body: WARN Could not load compiled rules ... is not valid JSON, RESULT { version: 1, rules: [] }. The loader behaviour predates B1; B1 inherited it and its changeset claimed a refusal on every path. FOLDED at 8a782608: the guard reads through the loader with an onWarn that throws TotemParseError (PARSE_FAILED) naming the file, before any write, on every path, and --allow-record-rows does not lift it; two tests written RED first (promise resolved on the pre-fold code); the stale comment at compile.ts ~921 that claimed the loader throws on malformed JSON corrected.
